query: I'm new to investing and have student loans. What should I prioritize first with my savings?

recommendations.title: Complete Emergency Fund Before Increasing Investments
recommendations.summary: Prioritize building your 6-month emergency fund ($22,000) in a high-yield savings account before making additional investment commitments.
recommendations.detailed_rationale: With $15,000 in cash (60% of $25,000), you're about 68% toward your $22,000 emergency fund goal. As a beginner investor with conservative risk tolerance, no emergency fund, moderate debt, and a loss comfort of only 3/10, financial stability must come first. Your current allocation is already appropriate (60% cash, 40% conservative investments), but you should complete the emergency fund in a HYSA earning 4-5% before adding to investment positions. This protects you from forced liquidation of investments during market downturns if unexpected expenses arise.
recommendations.suggested_action: Move existing cash to high-yield savings account and direct next $7,000 in savings to complete emergency fund

recommendations.title: Maintain Current Conservative Investment Mix
recommendations.summary: Keep your existing VTTSX and BND holdings unchanged while focusing on debt reduction and emergency fund completion.
recommendations.detailed_rationale: Your current 40% investment allocation (30% VTTSX target-date fund, 10% BND bonds) is well-suited to your conservative profile and beginner experience. VTTSX provides automatic diversification and rebalancing appropriate for someone in their late 20s. With your negative net worth (-$13,000) and moderate debt load ($38,000), you should not increase investment exposure now. These holdings can remain untouched and continue growing through potential employer matches or small contributions, but major new investment should wait until emergency fund is complete and high-interest debt is reduced.
recommendations.suggested_action: Hold current positions, make no additional purchases until emergency fund complete

recommendations.title: Accelerate High-Interest Debt Repayment
recommendations.summary: After completing emergency fund, aggressively pay down any debt with interest rates above 6% before expanding investments.
recommendations.detailed_rationale: With $38,000 in liabilities and monthly expenses of $3,800 against $72,000 income, you have approximately $900-1,000 monthly surplus after taxes and expenses. Student loans likely carry 4-7% interest rates. Once your emergency fund reaches $22,000, redirect surplus cash flow to eliminate any debt above 6% interest. This provides a guaranteed 'return' better than conservative investment options and reduces financial risk. For debt below 5%, minimum payments are acceptable while building house down payment. This debt reduction improves your net worth position and strengthens your mortgage application for your 5-7 year homeownership goal.
recommendations.suggested_action: After emergency fund completion, allocate $600-800/month to above-market-rate debt payoff

recommendations.title: Future House Down Payment Strategy in Conservative Bonds
recommendations.summary: After emergency fund and high-interest debt are addressed, allocate house savings to short-term bond funds and CDs for 5-7 year horizon.
recommendations.detailed_rationale: Your $60,000 house down payment goal with a 5-7 year timeline requires capital preservation over growth. Once emergency fund is complete and high-rate debt reduced (approximately 18-24 months from now), begin systematic contributions to short-term investment-grade bond funds or CD ladders. Consider adding VGSH (Vanguard Short-Term Treasury ETF) or high-yield CDs with 1-5 year maturities. This provides 3.5-5% returns with minimal volatility, appropriate for your conservative tolerance. Avoid equity exposure for house funds since you cannot afford a 20-30% market decline right before your purchase timeline. Start with $300-400/month once prerequisites are met.
recommendations.suggested_action: Begin implementation in 18-24 months; allocate future savings to short-term bonds and CDs
